# Rust-boundary teaching-diagnostics study

This informed source study follows the [ordinary #68 decision](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/68#issuecomment-6009785277).
It preserves nine separate, complete edition-2026 first projects and predictions
written before their commands. The reset variants are separate first controls,
not a repaired source. [Context](context.md) states the author's prior Issue,
code and specification access, the fixed local executable identities, the
constitutional limits and the lack of a blind model benchmark or proof claim.

[Original predictions](predictions-before.json), [first inventory](first-files.json)
and [pending record](session.pending.json) are unchanged. The [before capture](observations-before/capture.json)
indexes 21 actual calls: text and JSON checks for every project, plus three
successful small runs. Its raw stream files preserve the exact outputs.
[Before assessment](assessment-before.json) records the real prediction mistake:
the public unresolved-name diagnostic code is `unknown_name`, not the predicted
internal checker code `name`. Every predicted exit and original span matched.

| First source | Actual before observation |
| --- | --- |
| `classical-drop-controls` | Unused/wildcard Bit, ordinary copying and user-defined classical `drop` succeed; run returns `10` with weight 1. |
| `unresolved-classical-drop` | `drop(0)` is an unresolved name, without a checked quantum-argument judgment. |
| `unresolved-quantum-drop` | `drop(q)` retains the unresolved-name priority. |
| `user-quantum-drop` | A resolved Observe helper named `drop` uses explicit `discard`; check and run succeed, returning `0` with weight 1. |
| `local-drop-category` | A runtime Bit named `drop` is not callable; the category diagnostic wins. |
| `nested-unit-wildcard` | `_` cannot lose an owner nested as `(Bit,(Q<Unit>,Unit))`. |
| `nested-unit-scope` | The same nested zero-width ownership cannot disappear at scope end. |
| `reset-result-discarded` | `reset(q);` rejects because its result is a live quantum owner. |
| `reset-result-returned` | A helper returns the fresh reset owner; explicit measurement then returns `0` with weight 1. |

The deterministic run expectations are elementary controls stated before calls;
numerical execution is supplemental observation. This packet does not certify
source preservation, independent runtime correctness, a general physical law,
QS/PR/RS discharge or completion of #67/#68 and their child Issues. No standalone
release, borrowed access, generic QFT or maximum-size case is introduced.

The [after capture](observations-after/capture.json) adds the same 21 actual
calls using the parent's separately supplied fixed executable. The
[comparison](comparison-after.json) confirms unchanged exits, diagnostic codes,
original spans and non-message JSON fields. Eleven observations retain both raw
streams exactly; ten change only the five designated rejection explanations in
text/JSON. The local callable-category error remains byte-identical. All three
successful run distributions are unchanged. Conditional absent-builtin advice
does not allege quantum ownership for `drop(0)`; both resolved user-defined
`drop` controls remain valid.

The registered [session](session.json) contains 42 observations, with zero source
repairs. The original pending record, separately sealed before record, context,
predictions, sources and raw results remain unchanged. Selected CLI and native
digests were checked around every invocation; they identify local executable
bytes, not an authenticated build chain or a native runtime proof.
